name: James Tissot
bio: Jacques Joseph Tissot, better known as James Tissot, was a French painter, illustrator, and caricaturist. He was born to a drapery merchant and a milliner and decided to pursue a career in art at a young age, coming to incorporate elements of realism, early Impressionism, and academic art into his work. He is best known for a variety of genre paintings of contemporary European high society produced during the peak of his career, which focused on the people and women's fashion of the Belle Époque and Victorian England, but he would also explore many medieval, biblical, and Japoniste subjects throughout his life. His career included work as a caricaturist for Vanity Fair under the pseudonym of Coïdé.

paintings.title: The Shop Girl (Tissot)
paintings.story: The Shop Girl is an oil on canvas painting by French artist James Tissot, from 1883-1885. It is in the Art Gallery of Ontario, in Toronto.
facts: The painting depicts a young woman standing inside a shop selling ribbons and dresses.
In one hand she holds a wrapped package of newly purchased items.

paintings.title: The Gallery of H.M.S. 'Calcutta' (Portsmouth)
paintings.story: The Gallery of HMS 'Calcutta' (Portsmouth), also known as Officer and Ladies on Board HMS Calcutta, is an 1876 oil painting by the French artist James Tissot. It depicts two ladies in fashionable clothing and a young naval lieutenant, standing on the quarter gallery at the stern of the Royal Navy warship HMS Calcutta. The Tate Gallery in London holds the painting and measures 68.6 by 91.8 centimetres (27.0 in × 36.1 in).
facts: HMS Calcutta was an 84-gun second rate ship of the line, built from teak in Bombay in 1831.
After a period in reserve, she was recommissioned in 1855 to serve in the Baltic in the Crimean War, and then served in the Second Opium War in the Far East in 1856-8.

paintings.title: Portrait of Mademoiselle L.L.
paintings.story: Portrait of Mademoiselle L.L. is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1864. It depicts a young woman wearing a red bolero jacket seated on a small table. The initials in the title are now a mystery although the women had modelled for Tissot before.

paintings.title: Holyday (Tissot)
paintings.story: Holyday, later also known as The Picnic, is an oil painting by French painter James Tissot (1836–1902), painted in 1876. The composition is set in the artist’s garden in the wealthy north London suburb of St John’s Wood. Tissot moved to England in the year 1871, when he was thirty five and settled there. Before moving to London, Tissot was a successful painter of Paris society.
facts: A Convalescent is in the Manchester Art Gallery; Holyday was acquired by the Tate Gallery in 1928.
Holyday was painted in the back garden of Tissot's London home, near the Lord's Cricket Ground.

paintings.title: The Two Sisters (Tissot)
paintings.story: The Two Sisters is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1863.

paintings.title: Japanese Girl Bathing
paintings.story: Japanese Girl Bathing is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1864. It features a young Japanese nude woman bathing. The work was part of the nineteenth century tradition of orientalism. Tissot, who never visited Japan, painted a French model in his Parisian studio draped in a kimono. However, she wears it more like a European bathrobe. The theme of Japanese objects is a recurring theme in his work of this period.

paintings.title: Tea (James Tissot)
paintings.story: Tea is a mid-19th century painting by French artist James Tissot. Done in oil on wood, the painting depicts a scene in which a young woman reacts to word that a captain is departing. Tea is itself a repetition of the left-hand side of a larger work by Tissot, Bad News. The work is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

paintings.title: Portsmouth Dockyard (Tissot)
paintings.story: Portsmouth Dockyard is an oil painting on canvas by French artist James Tissot, from 1877. It is a reworking of his 1876 painting On The Thames, which also depicts a man and two women in a boat.
facts: The painting depicts three people sitting in a rowing boat among the towering naval vessels in Portsmouth Dockyard, with another rowing boat crewed by naval personnel passing in the background before the bows of two old-fashioned square rigged ships of the line.
In the centre is a man wearing the uniform of a sergeant in a Highland Regiment, with redcoat, kilt, and feather bonnet.

paintings.title: What Our Lord Saw from the Cross
paintings.story: What Our Lord Saw from the Cross is an watercolor painting by the French painter James Tissot, from c. 1890. It is held at the Brooklyn Museum, in New York
facts: The whole watercolor series, completed between 1886 and 1894, was acquired in 1900 by the Brooklyn Museum in New York.
The work is unusual for its portrayal of the Crucifixion of Jesus, seen from the perspective of Jesus on the cross, rather than featuring Christ at the center of the work.

paintings.title: Too Early
paintings.story: Too Early is an oil on canvas genre painting by the French artist James Tissot, from 1873.
facts: Today the painting is in the collection of the Guildhall Art Gallery, in the City of London, having been acquired in 1902 by a gift from Charles Gassiot.
It depicts a ballroom scene set in the fashionable Victorian high society with some of the guests, a father and his three daughters, having arrived embarrassingly early for the ball.

paintings.title: London Visitors
paintings.story: London Visitors is an oil on canvas genre painting by the French artist James Tissot, from 1874.
facts: Produced during his time in Britain, it depicts a number of visitors to the capital London shown at the portico entrance to the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square with St Martin-in-the-Fields in the background.
A couple are depicted discussing what to see next, she points with an umbrella while he consults a guidebook.

paintings.title: The Captain's Daughter (painting)
paintings.story: The Captain's Daughter is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1873.
facts: Today the painting is in the collection of the City Art Gallery in Southampton, having been acquired in 1934.

While the exact scene depicted is unclear, it appears that the younger man is attempting to unsuccessfully court the captain's daughter either because she is not interested or because her father is proving difficult to win over.

paintings.title: Waiting for the Ferry at the Falcon Tavern
paintings.story: Waiting for the Ferry at the Falcon Tavern is an oil on canvas genre painting by the French artist James Tissot, from 1874. It is held at the Speed Art Museum, in Louisville.
facts: It was produced during Tissot's time in Britain, where he had moved following the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War.
It depicts a scene that takes place at the dock at the rear of the Falcon Tavern in Gravesend on the River Thames.

paintings.title: An Interesting Story (painting)
paintings.story: An Interesting Story is an oil on panel genre painting by the French artist James Tissot, from 1872. It is held at the National Gallery of Victoria, in Melbourne.
facts: Today the work is in the National Gallery of Victoria, in Melbourne, having been acquired in 1938.
It depicts a scene in an English riverside tavern during the eighteenth century.

paintings.title: Hush! (painting)
paintings.story: Hush! is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1875.
facts: A genre painting it depicts a musical evening held at a salon in the fashionable London suburb of Kensington.
Tissot's painting draws on the polite social conventions of the Victorian era as those in a drawing room politely listening as young woman is about to play the violin accompanied by a piano.

paintings.title: The Farewells
paintings.story: The Farewells is an oil on canvas genre painting by the French artist James Tissot, from 1871.
facts: It depicts a young couple reluctantly saying their goodbyes through an iron gate and railings as they are holding hands.
The young girl seems nostalgic as she bids farewell to her beloved.

paintings.title: Waiting for the Train
paintings.story: Waiting for the Train is an oil painting on panel by the French artist James Tissot, from c. 1873. It is also known as Waiting for the Train . It is held at the Dunedin Public Art Gallery.
facts: The painting is at the Dunedin Public Art Gallery, which acquired it in 1921 through a bequest of some £90 from local art enthusiast Thomas Brown.
A genre painting, it depicts a fashionably dressed young woman waiting at Willesden Junction railway station in London surrounded by luggage.

paintings.title: Saint Joseph Seeks a Lodging at Bethlehem
paintings.story: Saint Joseph Seeks a Lodging at Bethlehem is an opaque watercolor painting over graphite by French artist James Tissot. The painting was created between 1886–1894, near the end of his career. It is held at the Brooklyn Museum, in New York. This style of painting is also known as Gouache.
facts: The painting depicts Mary and her husband, Joseph, looking for a room for the night.
Because of the Census of Caesar Augustus (also known as the Census of Quirinius), the town is overcrowded and there is no room to be had.

paintings.title: Portrait of Frederick Burnaby
paintings.story: Portrait of Frederick Burnaby is an oil on panel portrait painting by the French artist James Tissot from 1870. It depicts the British army officer and celebrity Frederick Burnaby.
facts: However, this portrait was commissioned by the politician and magazine publisher Thomas Gibson Bowles, a friend of Burnaby.
The painting is now in the collection of the National Portrait Gallery, in London, having been acquired in 1933.
The painting was the inspiration for the portrait The Brigadier (2003-2004), by Lucian Freud, where he depicts his friend Andrew Parker Bowles, in a pose inspired by Burnaby.

paintings.title: The Ball on Shipboard
paintings.story: The Ball on Shipboard is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1874. It is held at the Tate Britain, in London.
facts: The painting is in the Tate Britain, having been acquired via the Chantrey Bequest in 1937.
It shows a scene on the deck of a ship, festooned with flags during a regatta held off the Isle of Wight.

paintings.title: Young Women Looking at Japanese Articles
paintings.story: Young Women Looking at Japanese Articles is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1869.
facts: It depicts two young French woman peering curiously at artefacts acquired from Japan.
Today the painting is in the collection of Cincinnati Art Museum in Ohio, which acquired it in 1984.

paintings.title: The Last Evening (painting)
paintings.story: The Last Evening is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1873. It shows a scene set aboard a ship, but it is unclear exactly the context or the relationship between the various figures. It has occasionally been confused with another painting Tissot produced that year, The Captain's Daughter.

paintings.title: The Convalescent
paintings.story: The Convalescent is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1876.
facts: A genre painting it shows a young woman recovering from ill health drowsing while an older woman reads aloud to her.
It features Tissot's lover and frequent model Kathleen Newton, while the backdrop is the artist's own large garden at 17 Grove End Road in St John's Wood.

paintings.title: The Bunch of Lilacs
paintings.story: The Bunch of Lilacs is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist James Tissot, from 1875. It is held in a private collection.

paintings.title: Chichester Samuel Parkinson-Fortescue (1823–1898), Baron Carlingford and 2nd Baron Clermont
Porträt der Sydney Milner-Gibson
paintings.story: The portrait of Miss Milner-Gibson, daughter of Thomas Milner-Gibson, and granddaughter of Sir John Gery Cullum, 8th Bart., was commissioned by Miss Milner-Gibson's half-brother Thomas Bowles from his friend James Tissot. The artist Tissot, having fled France, lived for a time at Bowles' London home, and was accepting commissions for portraits. This portrait was willed to the Borough of St Edmundsbury by George Gery Milner-Gibson Cullum, last surviving member of the family, who left a large collection of paintings and decorative arts to the Borough.
